elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.2: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." Ono is our party; the Agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days advance written notice to Array" — the redacted [ * ] notice period and the delayed commencement tied to First Commercial Sale are both removed, so the right is exercisable at any time on 30 days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "Array shall refund to Ono, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." Pro rata basis is expressly stated (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), and the refund is tied to the convenience termination in the same Section.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No Array convenience right appears anywhere in the record: 13.1 permits earlier termination only "pursuant to this Article 13," and the reviewed Article 13 sections give Array only for-cause exits (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy), with 13.5 Safety/Efficacy exits reserved to Ono. Nothing in the redline creates an Array at-will exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause fixes notice at thirty (30) days, which is the preferred (shorter) period and outside the 60-90 day fallback band; the fallback offer appears only in the margin comment, not in operative language.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: rendered 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on Ono's convenience exit, so no cap is needed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply a fortiori: Array holds no convenience termination right at all under Article 13 as rendered, so no term-end limitation is required.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array has no convenience termination right, so no notice floor is engaged.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: an unconditional Ono election to terminate "for convenience at any time," 30 days' advance written notice, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no Array convenience exit anywhere in Article 13.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: ok=false" is a false negative on substance — the rendered 13.2 contains "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time... by giving thirty (30) days advance written notice." The regex result should not override the plain language; the remaining gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with completeness.

Fallback is incomplete only on the notice-period element (30 days rather than 60-90); this is immaterial because the proposal sits at the stronger preferred level, and the comment properly flags 60-90 days as a negotiable fallback rather than embedding it.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are the delayed-commencement trigger (the later of two redacted periods after First Commercial Sale) and the redacted notice period, both of which must go to reach the preferred notice and at-will elements. Customer-favourable and neutral retained language survives — the heading, "for any reasons," and the requirement that notice be accompanied by the rationale. The drafter correctly omitted the model-language surplus "in whole or in part," which is unnecessary absent an Order Form or partial-termination structure, and added no survival tail, procedure or boilerplate.

Intent is preserved: 13.1's term, Product-by-Product/country-by-country expiry, post-expiry licence conversion and trademark/domain rights are untouched; the for-cause (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Safety/Efficacy (13.5) mechanics and Section 8.2 remain operative and are not contradicted by an at-will Ono exit that 13.1 already contemplates ("unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13"). No dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is introduced.

Minor drafting point for the negotiator (rationale-level, not a defect requiring repair): this Agreement's economics are upfront/milestone/royalty payments rather than subscription "fees," so consider confirming that "fees prepaid by Ono" captures the intended prepaid amounts; as drafted it is workable and does not create an undefined term.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original 13.2 gave Ono no convenience right until the later of two redacted post-First-Commercial-Sale periods in a term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, i.e. no Customer convenience right for a multi-year stretch — walk-away territory — with a redacted notice period and no refund.
